inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement should be understood as a warning about years of unresolved obligations, not simply as union leaders holding students hostage. Students and families are right to worry about disruption, but blaming workers for using their collective leverage shifts attention from the government’s failure to meet its commitments. A just settlement must protect students’ education and workers’ rights—and address the institutional neglect that keeps turning disputes into crises.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is the predictable result of obligations left unresolved for years. It is easy to make workers the villains when students fear disruption, but that blame lets government off the hook for failing to honor its commitments. Students and workers are both being harmed by a system that treats education and labor rights as expendable. The answer is not to silence collective action; it is to meet the obligations and fix the institutional neglect that keeps pushing these disputes into crisis.
